title: Port Forwarding to 127.0.0.1 on Windows Host not working
body:
### Issue Description

I updated from Podman to Podman 6.0.2 and since then port forwarding to the windows host does not work anymore. It still works using the IP of the podman machine. Also running a server inside the podman machine without containers works correctly.

Even a clean installation of Podman 6.0.2 did not solve the issue.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1.  Run `podman run --rm -p 8080:80 nginx`
2. Run `Test-NetConnection 127.0.0.1 -Port 8080 ` (should not work)
3. Run `Test-NetConnection <wslip> -Port 8080 ` (should work)
4. Cancel execution
5. Run `podman machine ssh`
6. Run `python3 -m http.server 8080` inside podman machine (run directly without using containers)
7. Run `Test-NetConnection 127.0.0.1 -Port 8080 ` (should work)
8. Run `Test-NetConnection <wslip> -Port 8080 ` (should work)

### Describe the results you received

Test-NetConnection 127.0.0.1 -Port 8080 does not work for containers, works without containers

Test-NetConnection <wslip> -Port 8080 works for both ways

### Describe the results you expected

I would expect podman containers to be reachable from Windows host network.

I just downgraded to Podman CLI v5.8.5 and it works fine.

We switched the port forwarding logic to better bind the ports in https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/27311

The logic is actually required to properly work with ipv6 localhost connections and in general calling listen() on them was always wrong as we do not have actually logic to accept connections there which means the connections that ended up there (bypassing the firewall nat rules) would just hang.

So at least on the linux side I do not see us changing this by default. I guess we could consider adding an option to add the listen call back but I really like to avoid that if possible. A udp socket does not have listen() so how does the forwarding work there in WSL?

cc @l0rd @danishprakash

> A udp socket does not have listen() so how does the forwarding work there in WSL?

Doing a quick read of the WSL codebase I guess the answer is they do not support udp forwarding at all?
